solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stock colours

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, stock means usual, regular, as supplied by default
a regiment's colours are its flag or banner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Colours' is a plural, but in the military sense it names one flag, carried into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are synonyms: regular or ordinary goods, and a flag borne by a regiment.

clue.text: Trinity right within you

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the old pronoun

parts.note: thee is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A believer tells God that the Holy Trinity is rightly within them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts R inside THEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinity is a group of a trio, so it is the number after two.

clue.text: Introspection doing little to inspire government leader supporting church body

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting part goes below, so the church body comes first

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the idler takes the letter inside

parts.note: lazing means idling, doing little

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An idle official drawing breath beneath a church committee, absorbed in themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to inspire' means breathe in, so the idler takes in the leader's letter; 'supporting' in a down clue means sitting underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for excessive self-contemplation, staring at one's own belly button.

clue.text: A body builder's out-of-this-world body

parts.note: a steroid builds muscle, so it is a body builder; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A weightlifter's physique is out of this world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body builder' means a muscle-building drug, not a gym enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet orbiting the sun is a body literally beyond our world.

clue.text: Stop being a comedian? You can't be serious!

definitions.meaning: a plea to someone to cease cracking jokes

explanation.surface: Someone tells a would-be comic to give up the jokes and doubts they mean it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally asks a joker to stop, and idiomatically scoffs at a ridiculous claim.

clue.text: Warm and moist — like some marine life?

definitions.meaning: damp and sticky, as hands get when nervous
playfully read as 'clam-like', in the manner of a shellfish

explanation.surface: A muggy seaside day prompts the question of whether the weather resembles creatures of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a whimsical coinage, the question mark warning that it is not a dictionary meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym for sticky dampness, and jokingly an adjective formed from the bivalve's name.

clue.text: Cap of cerulean and gold on a crown

indicators.note: the cap of a word is its top letter, here the first in a down answer

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A blue and gold headpiece sits atop a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' looks like a hat to go with the crown; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word means crown, and names crown-like things such as the halo around the sun.

clue.text: A silencing word remains

parts.note: sh is said to make people be quiet

explanation.surface: Someone shushing a crowd says what is left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: what is left after burning.
explanation.definitionFit: The powder left after a fire is what remains, as in cremated remains.

clue.text: People ecstatic at first about party removing a PM

indicators.note: the people and the letter go round the party remnant

parts.note: men means people, as in 'officers and men'

indicators.note: the party loses the letter that follows

parts.note: Labour is a major British political party

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Delighted voters ditch their leader as the party ousts a Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first', 'removing' and 'about' work in turn, the people and letter wrapping the trimmed party. Lord Melbourne was Queen Victoria's first Prime Minister, and the Australian city is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Melbourne was a Whig Prime Minister of the 1830s, so he is an example of a PM.

clue.text: Evergreen power to fascinate

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
to rivet someone is to hold their attention completely

explanation.surface: Something always fresh has the power to captivate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen' looks like an adjective praising the power, but it is the noun: a hedging shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The hedge shrub keeps its leaves all year, so it is an example of an evergreen plant.

clue.text: Hydrogen expands in large flexible pipe

indicators.note: the gas swells into the middle of the letters, so the word signals going inside them
flexible letters bend into a new order, so the word signals an anagram

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: gas swells inside a big bendy tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' gives NARGILE, a spelling of the same pipe, and 'expands' fills it out with the gas after its G.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Middle Eastern water pipe, also called a hookah, where smoke is drawn through water.

clue.text: Thriving source of water

definitions.meaning: a shaft sunk to draw water from underground

explanation.surface: A spring that is flowing freely and doing nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is healthy or fine; the other is a hole bored down to reach groundwater.

clue.text: Deep thought: odd state to beset one

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so these letters go around the one

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange
a nation is a country or state
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A political musing: some peculiar country is about to besiege somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset' means surround, so the odd state closes round the numeral; 'rum' for odd is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means pondering at length, chewing something over in the mind, which is profound reflection.

clue.text: Ever maintaining rise during test, working on a plane, perhaps?

indicators.note: the combined letters come in the middle of the test

parts.note: a try is an attempt or test

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the poetic word holds the rise inside

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
a surge is a sudden rise

explanation.surface: An aircraft engineer keeps on climbing while trialling a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the tree, not an aircraft. 'maintaining' and 'during' nest one piece in another, giving TR + EESURGER + Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane is a kind of tree, so pruning or treating one is an example of this arboricultural work.

clue.text: Shrub, one beyond blight — job to contain it?

indicators.note: the job holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a task is a piece of work, a job

indicators.note: one comes after the blight, so the single letter follows it

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or blight
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether keeping a shrub's disease in check is a job of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beyond' places one after the blight, and 'to contain' splits the job after its second letter; 'it' refers back to that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: This feathery-leaved bush of salty and dry ground is an example of a shrub.

clue.text: Shiite leader always put on a ring, I see!

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is put on another piece sits above it

parts.note: ay is an old and poetic word for always
to toll is to ring a bell
ah is an exclamation of understanding

explanation.surface: Someone realises that the cleric always wears a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like jewellery but is the verb, as of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iranian religious title for a senior cleric, so a leader of Shia Islam.

clue.text: Peer in organ loft, but not very many times

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

indicators.note: the words say to keep the loft without the part named next

parts.note: oft is an old word for often, many times

explanation.surface: Someone peers from the organ gallery in church, though rarely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb, to look, but is the noun, a nobleman. 'but not' strips OFT from LOFT, leaving L.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman, a rank of the peerage.

clue.text: Nuclear accident in British base

parts.note: base means mean or contemptible, which is what a lowdown trick is

explanation.surface: A reactor mishap at a British military installation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military base but is the adjective, contemptible.
explanation.definitionFit: The technical term for a sudden rupture of a reactor's coolant system is a kind of nuclear accident.

clue.text: Monkey lives around borders of Kenya, to the west

indicators.note: in an across answer going west means reading right to left
the verb wraps round the edge letters of the country

parts.note: is means exists or lives

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A monkey living in the western border regions of Kenya.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders of', 'around' and 'to the west' work in turn: the inner step gives IKAS, which reads backwards in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-tailed South American primate is a kind of monkey.

clue.text: Syrup — huge number of lemmings initially stuck in it

indicators.note: the two letters are lodged inside the big number

parts.note: masses means a great quantity

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A horde of lemmings caught in sticky syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes O and L from 'of lemmings', and 'stuck in' puts them inside MASSES after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark sticky by-product of sugar refining is a syrup, called treacle in Britain.

clue.text: Failing to change sides

definitions.meaning: a noun, a flaw or shortcoming
to desert one cause or country for another

explanation.surface: Losing out makes someone switch allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a flaw or imperfection; as a verb it means abandoning one side for the enemy.

clue.text: Poet who's evidently been on the rack?

definitions.text: Poet who's evidently been on the rack?

parts.words: Poet who's evidently been on the rack?
parts.note: the rack stretched its victims, so someone who has been on it would be a tall, stretched man; this American poet's surname says exactly that

explanation.surface: A tortured poet, apparently literally so.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow wrote 'The Song of Hiawatha'; the clue reads his name as describing a stretched man.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineteenth-century American author of 'Hiawatha' is a poet, and his surname splits into a tall man.

clue.text: In conversation, bound to be engrossed

indicators.note: words in conversation are spoken, so we want something that sounds like the word

parts.note: bound means tied up or wrapped

explanation.surface: Talking, someone is certain to become absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to be' reads as 'certain to be', but 'bound' is the word that is said and 'to be' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entirely absorbed or fascinated by something is a synonym for being engrossed.

clue.text: After uprising, some mutual appreciation for island republic

indicators.note: After uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: After a revolt, a small island nation earns some shared admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'island republic'; 'for' is a link. 'some' takes UALAP from the phrase, and 'After uprising' reads it upwards, as suits a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific archipelago east of the Philippines is an independent island republic.

clue.text: Torch, a virtually full beam lit up

indicators.note: lit up suggests drunk, so the letters stagger into a new arrangement
virtually means almost, so the word is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: A torch shining a near full-beam light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims FULL to FUL, and 'lit up' rearranges A, FUL and BEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, especially one made of several thick waxed wicks.

clue.text: Chairman, on agonising march, heads northward

indicators.note: in a down answer going north means reading from bottom to top
the heads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: The Chairman leads his followers north on the gruelling Long March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' takes O, A and M, and 'northward' reverses them. The Long March of 1934 to 1935 did head north.
explanation.definitionFit: Mao Zedong was known as Chairman Mao, head of the Chinese Communist Party.

clue.text: Only rotten plays were written by him

definitions.note: a description standing for a playwright's name, the noun the answer is

parts.note: one can mean the only, as in 'my one hope'
feeling rotten means feeling ill

explanation.surface: A harsh critic's verdict: the man wrote nothing but bad plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill was the American playwright of 'Long Day's Journey into Night'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American Nobel-winning dramatist wrote many stage works, so he is a man by whom plays were written.

clue.text: Passage which crosses river, ending in Idaho

indicators.note: the pronoun spans across the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns

indicators.note: the last letter of the state name is taken

explanation.surface: A route that crosses a river and finishes in Idaho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending in' gives O, and 'crosses' puts R and O inside THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The throat is the passage in the neck leading to the stomach and lungs.

clue.text: Sweet tune recalled by one in French

parts.note: to hone a thing is to sharpen or fine-tune it

indicators.note: called back, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: un is French for one

explanation.surface: A sweet melody remembered by a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tune' is a verb here, to refine, not a melody. 'recalled' turns BY into YB.
explanation.definitionFit: As a term of endearment, like darling, it is what you might call your sweet; it is also a sticky pastry.
